ranked_evidence.title: Agriculture Ministry official denies claims of 50 million dogs in Egypt - Egypt Independent
ranked_evidence.snippet: The Director General of the General Administration for Licensing and Dealing with Dangerous Animals at the Egyptian Agriculture Ministry, Hind al-Sheikh, debunked claims of there being “50 million dogs” in Egypt and warned against spreading misinformation. During a Friday phone interview on the “al-Hekaya” (The Story) show, hosted by Amr Adib on MBC Masr, Sheikh noted that the presence of domestic dogs helps protect citizens from other dangers, such as reptiles and other pests. She added that dogs have been present in Egypt since the time of the Pharaohs, reflecting that addressing this issue requires time and comprehensive plans, not quick fixes. Sheikh affirmed that the state is implementing a unified national plan to manage the issue of stray animals, including free-roaming dogs, in coordination with all relevant authorities. The ministry is addressing the issue with a comprehensive and multifaceted approach, she assured, stressing that protecting citizens is a priority and that the problem is being addressed through sustainable solutions, not temporary measures.

ranked_evidence.title: A Major Ocean Current Is On The Verge of Collapse. Scientists Say The Effects May Reach California - ScienceAlert
ranked_evidence.snippet: # A Major Ocean Current Is On The Verge of Collapse. Dust from North Africa's Sahara Desert drifts thousands of miles to fuel food webs in the Amazon and the ocean's depths, while pollution-eating microbes hitch a ride through the atmosphere on gusts of wind or wisps of fog. The latest effort to iron out our understanding of the AMOC and the consequences of its stalling comes in the form of a study published in *Nature Communications*. "It is well known that the AMOC is a big player in the world's climate system, and that it is slowing down," says Mohima Mimi, a climate dynamics researcher at the University of California, Riverside, and the study's lead author. "It turns out a weakening AMOC will strengthen storms across parts of North America by the end of the century, along the California coast in particular, while reducing them over Greenland and the Arctic.". "In California, atmospheric rivers are a double-edged sword," Mimi says.

ranked_evidence.title: Fire captain, wife, 3 sons found dead after flash flood in Utah canyon; daughter is family's sole survivor - CBS News
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Fire captain, wife, 3 sons found dead after flash flood in Utah canyon; daughter is family's sole survivor. Five family members who had set out for a day of hiking were killed after a flash flood swept through canyons of southern Utah on Friday, law enforcement officials said. The victims were a captain in the Provo, Utah, fire department, his wife and their sons, according to fire officials. Although the sheriff's office did not identify the victims, the Provo Fire Department confirmed in a social media post that a fire captain, Spencer Long, and his family members were killed. Long, his wife Katrina and their sons Reid, Thayne and Gage died in the devastating floods, according to a GoFundMe site set up by a family friend to support the Longs' daughter as she navigates the loss of her family. "Our Provo Fire family is heartbroken to lose Captain Spencer Long, his wife Katrina, and their three sons Reid, Thayne and Gage due to a devastating flash flood Thursday evening," the fundraise page reads.

The Wayne County Sheriff's Office said they responded to the Sunglow Campground Area in Bicknell, Utah, after getting a report that a body had been found. A GoFundMe created in honor of the family said Long, his wife Katrina and their sons Reid, Thayne and Gage died due to devastating flash floods.

ranked_evidence.snippet: # Senior Shelter Dog Spends His Golden Years in Cold & Hard Kennel Instead of Loving Home. He still lights up every time his favorite volunteer appears, even after spending well over a year at the shelter. His face has gone gray, his steps have slowed a little, and lately he hasn’t been feeling well, but none of that has changed the way he greets people. The video opens with Charlie standing inside his kennel, wearing a colorful bandana and wagging happily as he spots a familiar volunteer. Although the shelter currently recommends that he be the only pet, the in-video caption suggests that with patience, he may be able to coexist with another dog. We also get to see the most gorgeous still photo of Charlie’s frosty face before the caption reads, “My face may be frosty.” Seconds later, he gallops towards his favorite volunteer for a hug as another line appears: “But I will be your joy.” You can’t help but feel his happiness through the clip.
